clue.text: Taxi Driver, for example, dropping straight outside international court

parts.note: a dropping, like a motion, is a lump of excrement

indicators.note: outside says the word for straight goes around the letters for international court

parts.note: straight in the sense of undiluted, pure

explanation.surface: Travis Bickle's cab seems to be shedding something outside a world court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' looks like a verb but is a noun: a dropping and a motion are both bowel matter. 'straight' is undiluted, as in a straight whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi Driver is Scorsese's 1976 film, an example of a movie.

clue.text: Mean policeman with attitude to race?

parts.note: the mean is the middle value
DI is a Detective Inspector
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A surly cop with a chip on his shoulder about some race issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like ethnicity in the surface; the question mark flags that it is an athletics event, defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle distance is an athletics category, so a race over 800 or 1500 metres is an example of it.

clue.text: Fool hiding small kink

indicators.note: hiding means the word for fool conceals the small letter inside it

parts.note: a twit is a fool
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An idiot concealing a minor perversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a bend or kink, as in a hose or a rope.

clue.text: Doctor Who and Davros absorbing essence of Red Dwarf

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter is taken

explanation.surface: Science-fiction television mash-up: Doctor Who and his foe Davros meeting the sitcom Red Dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who, Davros (the Daleks' creator) and Red Dwarf are all British TV sci-fi; only 'Dwarf' is the definition, as a verb. WHO, DAVROS and E (centre of RED) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to make it seem small by comparison, which is exactly what overshadowing does.

clue.text: Two chums having webbed feet

parts.note: a pal is a chum
the second of the two chums: a mate is also a friend

explanation.surface: A pair of friends who share a peculiar trait: webbed feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two chums' supplies two words for a friend, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmate describes a duck's foot: toes joined by webbing, shaped like an open hand.

clue.text: Number one fast food staple? Hamburger's a favourite, ultimately

parts.note: cod is the fish in a British fish-and-chip supper, a staple takeaway
a person from Hamburg would say ein for 'a'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of favourite

explanation.surface: Fast-food talk: whether fish is the top takeaway choice and the burger a favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that numbs, not a figure. 'Hamburger' is a person from Hamburg, so German EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is a painkilling drug, so it deadens pain: a thing that numbs, read as num-ber.

clue.text: Lastly, you mentioning occupational injury is threatening

indicators.note: Lastly asks for the final letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Someone bringing up a workplace injury claim, perhaps with menace.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly mood or situation is one that is hostile and menacing.

clue.text: Banishment from unisex pool arranged after dropping a zip

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order
dropping means these letters are taken out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: zip is nothing, zero, which is the letter O

explanation.surface: Being thrown out of a mixed swimming pool for losing a zip.
explanation.walkthrough: UNISEX POOL has ten letters; take away one O (a zip, nothing) and the remaining nine are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Expulsion is the act of forcing someone out, a formal banishment.

clue.text: Questionable Lib Dem plan not including university for Harlow, famously?

indicators.note: a questionable plan is dubious, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Political sniping at a doubtful Liberal Democrat policy that leaves out universities, set in Harlow, an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlow looks like the Essex new town, but it is the 1930s film star Jean Harlow. The letters of LIB DEM PLAN NOT, plus U, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Harlow was nicknamed the Platinum Blonde after her 1931 film of that name and her famous white-blonde hair.

clue.text: Verdi composed lines — adding finishing touches for The Leopard made little sense

indicators.note: composed means the letters of Verdi are rearranged, apt for a composer

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: finishing touches are the final letters of The and Leopard

explanation.surface: Verdi writing music for The Leopard, Visconti's film of Lampedusa's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange VERDI to DRIVE, add LL, then E and D, the last letters of THE and LEOPARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to talk nonsense, so someone who drivelled spoke without making sense.

clue.text: Call publisher originally to replace book jacket's design feature?

indicators.note: to replace means the publisher's first letter goes where the book letter stood

parts.note: to label something is to call it a name

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of publisher

explanation.surface: A publisher asked to swap a feature of a book's dust-jacket design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book jacket' looks like one phrase, but 'book' belongs to the wordplay: in LABEL the B gives way to P.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap at the front of a coat or jacket, a feature of its tailoring.

clue.text: Auction item with American sports car

parts.note: a lot is an item for sale at an auction
US is short for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A classic American sports car going under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British maker of sports cars, such as the Elise and Esprit.

clue.text: A short ruler's similar

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A remark about a ruler of small stature being alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or of a similar kind.

clue.text: Matt fixed puncture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... paint finish is matt, not shiny
second meaning: a ... fee or rate is fixed

explanation.walkthrough: Matt looks like a man's name repairing a tyre; it is the paint finish, and each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a dull surface finish, an unvarying charge, and a deflated tyre.

clue.text: Sportsman's warning over athlete's predecessor

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn others of a ball in flight
a runner is an athlete

explanation.surface: A golfer's shout ringing out above a sprinter's precursor.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner is someone or something that comes before, a precursor.

clue.text: State of Delaware ignoring Washington over carbon

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the trimmed word goes over the carbon letter
ignoring means those letters are left out of Delaware

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: US geography: one state named in preference to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a US state to match Delaware and Washington; it is the verb. DELARE covers C.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to state something formally or openly.

clue.text: Generous promises to pay after limit placed on account

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed on means put above the next piece
after means this piece follows the others

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Banking: a borrowing cap set on an account after IOUs pile up.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous helping or room is roomy and ample, which is capacious.

clue.text: Wearing down gearbox occasionally — is reversing working

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter
reversing means the word is is read backwards, fitting a gearbox

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A car's gearbox wearing out when the vehicle is put in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of a surface, by water, wind or friction.

clue.text: Guess it's sugar making middle of ice-cream very soft

indicators.note: making says the central letters are turned into something else

parts.note: sucrose is ordinary table sugar

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of ice-cream

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft

explanation.surface: A cook guessing that sugar is what makes the ice-cream so soft.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of ICECREAM is CR; in SUCROSE those letters become PP.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or conjecture without certainty.

clue.text: In hotel it is totally snobbish

indicators.note: In signals the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A verdict on a posh hotel: everything about it is snooty.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours a select superior group, so the adjective means snobbish.

clue.text: Problem with seabird penetrating bone

indicators.note: penetrating means the bird goes inside the word for problem

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird with a beak stuck in a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone in the middle of the chest.

clue.text: Abridge Sherlock Holmes, initially on Gold, and on catch up

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of Sherlock and Holmes

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Cutting down a Sherlock Holmes story about gold and a fishing catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, to make it shorter.

clue.text: Start to record with two taps after introduction to Amazon Prime

indicators.note: after means the record letter and taps follow the Amazon letter
introduction to means the first letter of Amazon, which leads the answer
Start to means the first letter of record, placed after the Amazon letter

parts.note: C and H are the cold and hot markings on taps

explanation.surface: Recording a show on Amazon Prime with a couple of clicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon Prime' reads as the streaming service, but 'Prime' is the definition. Two taps are C and H, for cold and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-rival, so prime.

clue.text: Use cipher once to follow agents' farewell

indicators.note: to follow means the zero comes after the agency

parts.note: CIA is the American intelligence agency, its agents
a cipher is a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Spies using a one-time code to say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an informal Italian goodbye, also used in English.

clue.text: Regularly visiting guest, unable to get regular order

indicators.note: Regularly means taking every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: A frequent visitor who can't get their normal order.
explanation.walkthrough: Take alternate letters of GUEST UNABLE, starting with the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual is the drink or meal a regular customer habitually orders.

clue.text: Peacekeepers and press wanting right association

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeepers

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: UN forces and the media lacking a right-wing link.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together of people or groups, an alliance.

clue.text: Writer's stomach churning dash

indicators.note: the stomach of a word is its middle, and churning stirs those central letters so they change places

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: An author feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: A biro is a ballpoint pen; only its middle two letters IR swap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and dash, liveliness of style.

clue.text: Singers some paper reported

indicators.note: reported signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A newspaper's report on a group of singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests a newspaper, but it is a measure of sheets; quire sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of people who sing together.

clue.text: Aim to have unconfined lions in big top's opening

indicators.note: opening means those words come first, before the trimmed lions

parts.note: the big top is a circus tent

indicators.note: unconfined means the outer letters are removed

explanation.surface: A circus ringmaster's plan to let lions roam free in the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is a plan or purpose one means to carry out.

clue.text: Old lady getting into smack on get away — arms are used here

indicators.note: on means this piece follows the first

parts.note: shoo is said to tell someone to get away

indicators.note: getting into means the gran goes inside the word for smack

parts.note: a smack of something is a tinge or trace
a gran is a grandmother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A granny slapping someone telling them to scram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' looks like a slap but means a slight flavour or trace, as in 'a smack of garlic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearms are fired at targets on a shooting range, where weapons practice takes place.
